content.text:
Confirmed: before commit a7d58052 there was no such block at all — it went straight from `init(myDataChoices)` to the "Check if we have been removed" section. The commit a7d58052 inserted the new time-driver logic block that directly dereferences `myDataChoices` without a null guard, which is exactly the code the fix commit wraps in `if (myDataChoices != null)`.

## Bug-Introducing Commits
BIC: a7d580522c762178aadcef72f72ba46a34a5b798

## Reasoning

**(1) Investigation:** I looked at the fix diff, which wraps a block of code (accessing `myDataChoices.size()`, `myDataChoices.get(0)`, etc.) inside a new `if (myDataChoices != null)` guard, inside `DisplayControlImpl.init(...)`. To find when this unguarded block was introduced, I used `git log -S"myDataChoices.get(0) instanceof DerivedDataChoice"` (pickaxe search) on the file's history (following it through a directory rename from `ucar/...` to `src/ucar/...`). This located exactly two commits touching that string: the rename commit `115dc55a` (which is just a `git mv`, not a real content change) and `a7d580522c762178aadcef72f72ba46a34a5b798`, authored by Yuan Ho on 2011-11-02.

**(2) The specific change:** Commit `a7d58052` inserted a brand-new block right after the `if (!init(myDataChoices)) {...}` call:
```java
if(myDataChoices.size() > 0 && myDataChoices.get(0) instanceof DerivedDataChoice){
    List cdcs = ((DerivedDataChoice)myDataChoices.get(0)).getChoices();
    ...
}
```
Before this commit, the code went directly from the `init(myDataChoices)` call to the `//Check if we have been removed` section — there was no code here that dereferenced `myDataChoices` at all. This new block calls `myDataChoices.size()` without checking whether `myDataChoices` is `null`. Since `myDataChoices` can be set to `null` (e.g., in the `doRemove()`/cleanup path, `myDataChoices = null;`, `DisplayControlImpl.java:7027`) — plausibly via a concurrent removal (`hasBeenRemoved`) while `init()` is still running — this newly added block is capable of throwing a `NullPointerException`.

**(3) Supporting evidence:** 
- The pre-image of the file at `a7d58052~1` shows no such block existed.
- Every subsequent commit touching this code (`36d2a172`, `88443876`) only did cosmetic edits (spacing, comment toggling, brace addition) without adding the null check.
- The fix commit `b0c5379f` adds exactly `if (myDataChoices != null) { ... }` around this same block and nothing else, confirming the root cause is the missing null check introduced when the block was first written.

I'm confident in this attribution since the pickaxe search cleanly isolates a single content-introducing commit, and the before/after diffs directly corroborate the causal chain.
